authority: Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA)

description.en: The National Pension System (NPS) is a voluntary, defined-contribution retirement savings scheme regulated by PFRDA. It offers two types of accounts: Tier I (mandatory pension account with restrictions on withdrawal) and Tier II (voluntary savings with flexible withdrawal). NPS provides market-linked returns through professionally managed pension funds investing in equity, corporate bonds, government securities, and alternative assets.

verifiedConditions.claim: Any Indian citizen (resident or NRI) between 18 and 70 years of age can open an NPS Tier I account. The age limit was raised from 65 to 70 years in 2021.
The applicant must be KYC compliant with valid identity proof (Aadhaar, PAN) and address proof.

unverifiedEligibility: NRIs can join NPS subject to RBI and FEMA regulations. Contributions must be made through NRE/NRO accounts.
OCI (Overseas Citizen of India) cardholders are not eligible for NPS.
Government employees may be covered under NPS mandatorily if they joined service after January 1, 2004.

requirements.claim: Aadhaar number is required for eNPS online registration and Aadhaar-based e-KYC authentication. For offline registration, Aadhaar is accepted as identity and address proof.
PAN card is mandatory for NPS registration. eNPS allows PAN-based online registration as an alternative to Aadhaar-based registration.
Active savings bank account with IFSC code for initial contribution payment and subsequent transactions.
Active mobile number and email address for OTP verification and communication regarding the NPS account.
Initial contribution of minimum Rs. 500 for Tier I account opening. There is no maximum limit on contributions. Minimum annual contribution to keep the account active is Rs. 1,000.
Scanned photograph (for online registration) or passport-size photographs (for offline registration at Point of Presence).
Scanned signature (for online registration) or specimen signature on the registration form (for offline registration).

processInformation.claim: Register online through eNPS portal (enps.nsdl.com) using Aadhaar-based e-KYC or PAN verification, or visit a Point of Presence (PoP) — banks and designated service centres — to register offline with physical documents.

After successful KYC verification, a Permanent Retirement Account Number (PRAN) is generated. For online (Aadhaar-based) registration, PRAN is generated instantly. For PAN-based or offline registration, PRAN generation may take 2-7 working days.

Choose a Pension Fund Manager (PFM) and investment choice — Active Choice (allocate among equity E, corporate bonds C, government securities G, and alternative assets A within prescribed limits) or Auto Choice (lifecycle fund that automatically adjusts allocation based on age).
Make the initial contribution of minimum Rs. 500 via net banking, UPI, or debit card for online registration. For offline registration, payment can be made at the Point of Presence.

output.claim: A Permanent Retirement Account Number (PRAN) is issued — a unique 12-digit number that remains with the subscriber throughout their lifetime. A PRAN card (physical or e-PRAN) is dispatched to the registered address. The account can be accessed through the CRA (Central Recordkeeping Agency) system for contributions, fund switches, and withdrawals.

fees.claim: NPS registration is free. There are no account opening charges. The only requirement is the minimum initial contribution.

fees.applicability: Minimum initial contribution for Tier I
fees.claim: Minimum initial contribution of Rs. 500 for Tier I account. Minimum annual contribution is Rs. 1,000 to keep the account active. For Tier II, minimum initial contribution is Rs. 1,000.

processingTime.claim: Aadhaar-based eNPS registration generates PRAN instantly. PAN-based online registration takes 2-7 working days as physical documents need to be couriered to the CRA. Offline registration at Point of Presence takes 3-7 working days for PRAN generation.

limitations: This record does not cover NPS exit and withdrawal rules, partial withdrawal conditions, or annuity purchase requirements in detail.
Fund performance and returns are market-linked and not guaranteed.
Tax treatment details (Section 80CCD) are summarised; consult the Income Tax Act for full provisions.
Government employee NPS (mandatory) may have different operational rules than private sector or individual NPS.
NRI-specific rules and FEMA compliance requirements are not covered in detail.
